notes:
- A mailbox your agent could not read is now reported as exactly that, with what the mail provider
  said about it. An expired sign-in, a permission a workplace withdrew, or Outlook having a bad
  minute all used to arrive looking identical to a quiet morning: "the inbox is empty".
- Connecting an email account opens the mailbox once, straight away, while you are still sitting
  there. If it will not open, nothing is connected and the screen says what the provider said,
  instead of leaving a green row that never works.
- Your agent no longer insists it can read a mailbox that has never once opened. It used to be told
  to say it had access on the strength of the permissions alone, so it argued with people whose
  mail it genuinely could not reach.
- An Outlook account at a company or school whose administrator has to approve Archie now names the
  setting to ask for, spelled the way their admin console spells it, and where it lives. Asking an
  IT department to "approve an app called Archie" gets a reply asking which permission and where.
- The calendar is offered whichever email you use. That button was tied to Google being configured,
  so somebody connecting Outlook was never offered a calendar at all.
- Searching the store for "outlook" finds the email and calendar add-ons. Every one of them names
  both providers now, and Email Manager and Calendar answer to "outlook" spoken aloud as well.
- The store says which add-ons need an AI account of your own on the row, before you press Install,
  rather than refusing after you have pressed it.
- Two guides that did not exist. One is how to update Archie. The other is connecting your email and
  calendar: where the button is, what each permission lets your agent do, what to send a workplace
  administrator when it refuses, and what to do when an account stops working.
- The first-run screens say what Archie needs to run: this computer left awake and plugged into
  power, with the sleep setting named and where to change it, and a cable from your router if you
  can reach one. A routine set for 7:30am needs this computer awake at 7:30am.
- "Needs attention" is a button. It was two words beside a small icon whose only explanation was a
  tooltip, so there was nothing to press and, on a touchscreen, nothing to read.
- Six screens sent you to Settings to connect an email or calendar account. That is not where it
  is. They name the Connections tab, the section inside it, and the button, and they say to tick
  the permissions before you sign in.
- Fixed: an error that said only that something had failed now says where to go and what to press.
  A refused key names the screen you paste it into; a lost connection names the cable to check.
- Fixed: running out of credit on your own AI account names that company and its billing page. It
  used to send you to a company you may not have an account with.
